proxy_language: Proto-Afroasiatic / Proto-Semitic (with Proto-Natufian-era Levantine substrate as unattested background)
proxy_rationale: Khiamian (c. 10,000-9,500 BCE cal., Early PPNA, Levant) is known only archaeologically (El-Khiam points, Jericho, Mureybet, Nahal Oren). No language is attested. Following Militarev, Blench and Ehret, the Natufian/Epipaleolithic Levant is a candidate region for a Proto-Afroasiatic or early Semitic-ward dialect, but the linkage is very weak and the date (c. 7,000 years before Akkadian) is immense. The most defensible proxy is Proto-Semitic reconstruction notation (consonantal roots, CVC patterns) used as a stylistic stand-in, avoiding any pretense of attestation. Any name is a reconstruction-flavored construct, not a recorded word.
phonology: Proto-Semitic (Huehnergard/Kogan style): consonants *p *b *t *d *k *g *q (ejective) *ʔ *s *z *š *ṣ (emphatic) *ṯ *ḏ *ṱ (interdentals) *ḫ *ġ *ḥ *ʕ *h *m *n *l *r *w *y. Vowels *a *i *u with length (*ā *ī *ū); diphthongs *ay *aw. Emphatic series (ejectives) *ṭ *ṣ *q *ṱ. Lateral *ś (*ɬ) and *ṣ́ (*ɬʼ). No *e or *o.
phonotactics: Roots are triconsonantal (some biconsonantal, quadriliteral rarer). Syllable shapes CV, CVC, CVː; no initial vowels (initial glottal stop *ʔ counts as C); no initial consonant clusters; medial CC only across a syllable boundary (CVC.CV); word-final CC is rare; stress is not written. Words are typically 2-3 syllables.
orthography: Standard Semitist reconstruction transliteration with asterisks in scholarly use. For game names, plain Latin with a restricted set of diacritics: š ṣ ṭ ḥ ʕ ʔ ḫ ṯ ḏ ġ ā ī ū. Apostrophe/ʔ for glottal stop, ʕ written as ʿ if desired.
morphology: Root-and-pattern (templatic) morphology: root C1C2C3 + vocalic pattern (e.g. qatl, qitl, qutl nouns; maqtal place nouns; qattāl agent/occupation nouns; taqtil/taqtul abstract). Nominal suffixes: *-um nominative, *-im genitive, *-am accusative (mimation, Proto-Semitic); *-at feminine; dual *-ān/-ayn; plural *-ūm/-āt. Prefix *ma- for place/instrument nouns; *ta- for abstract; *ʔa- for adjectives of color/defect pattern *ʔaqtal.
compounding: Genitive construct state: head noun first, then dependent in the genitive (X-um Y-im, or reduced in names to X Y). 'X of Y' = X + Y (construct, head initial). Agent nouns by the qattāl pattern or participle qātil. Place names with prefix ma- (maqtal). Relational nisba suffix *-iy. No productive free compounding of the Indo-European type; compounds are construct phrases.
noun_phrase_order: Head noun first; genitive dependent follows the head; adjectives follow the noun and agree in gender/number/definiteness; numerals precede or follow depending on reconstruction.
sources: Kogan, Leonid. Genealogical Classification of Semitic (2015)
Bar-Yosef, Ofer. Natufian and PPNA cultural studies (various)
Blench, Roger. Archaeology and Language: Afroasiatic (various)
notes: Khiamian is a purely archaeological culture with no language attested. All names are speculative reconstruction-flavored forms in a Proto-Semitic-style template, not real attested words. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word unless the language is Goidelic (it is not here). Treat name output as stylization.
